headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and overlapping browser/network surfaces create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; TREK’s sensitive travel data raises compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx can observe Claude Code post-tool events and uses MCP/stdio plus filesystem, while TREK is a real-time collaborative app with MCP and browser surfaces. That creates a plausible default bridge where TREK content or shared files can be treated as instructions by ctx. The interaction is documented only by profiles, so uncertainty stays medium rather than low.
conditions: IF ctx reads TREK-generated files or MCP messages as trusted instructions
IF TREK content is copied into ctx-observed tool outputs without provenance tagging
mitigations: Disable shared MCP channels between the agents
Separate their workspaces and mount points
Add provenance labels to all TREK-originated content
Require manual review before ctx acts on TREK text
requires-engineering: enforce instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly touches reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, while ctx touches audit/runtime logs and filesystem data. Because both expose filesystem and MCP surfaces, a shared workspace can leak sensitive travel data into ctx logs or outputs. The blast radius includes secrets and account data, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents share ./data, uploads, or another common filesystem path
IF ctx logs or forwards TREK files, reservations, or secrets into audit/runtime logs
mitigations: Use separate per-agent directories
Redact secrets before any handoff
Restrict ctx from reading TREK uploads and databases
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets
requires-engineering: add access controls and DLP at the orchestrator boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances, and both can write to filesystem-backed state; TREK also has real-time collaborative behavior. Without explicit locking or isolation, concurrent writes to shared files or MCP state can race and corrupt work products. The profiles do not prove unrestricted same-dir writes, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same filesystem path or database
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking around shared MCP or file resources
mitigations: Assign disjoint writable directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent runs on shared resources
Check in changes through one agent only
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a collaborative travel planner with AI built in, and ctx observes tool events and manages context. If TREK output is fed into ctx or vice versa without verification, one agent can amplify the other’s mistakes into downstream actions or logs. The profiles suggest the pathway but do not show direct action authority, so medium fits.
conditions: IF TREK-generated plans are consumed by ctx without a verification step
IF ctx-produced summaries are used by TREK as authoritative inputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require citations or source links for all transferred facts
Mark agent outputs as untrusted by default
Limit downstream actions to read-only previews
requires-engineering: add validation gates before any automated action

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles reservations, documents, photos, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, which can include regulated or highly sensitive personal data. ctx also touches audit/runtime logs and filesystem data, so pairing them can create retention and residency mismatches if TREK data is logged or copied into ctx. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so high is prudent.
conditions: IF TREK data is copied into ctx logs or retained beyond TREK policy
IF any EU or regulated personal data is processed by both agents under different retention rules
mitigations: Minimize retained logs
Exclude secrets from shared outputs
Document a single retention policy for both agents
Purge copied travel records after use
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
